content: 1. Rilpivirine should be administered either 2 hours before or several hours after the administration of didanosine oral solution or chewable tablets. No dose adjustment is required when rilpivirine is co-administered with didanosine. 2. Didanosine must be taken on an empty stomach, at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine, which should be taken with a meal. 3. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of disopyramide by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring is required. 4. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 5. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dofetilide by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dolasetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring is required. 8. Donepezil and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Doxepin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dronedarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Droperidol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Efavirenz decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Efavirenz and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Eliglustat and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Elivaldogene autotemcel and rilpivirine may reduce each other’s effects. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least 1 month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 16. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete HIV regimen and should not be co-administered with rilpivirine or other antiretrovirals. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Encorafenib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Entrectinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Eribulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Erythromycin base increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases erythromycin base toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 21. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases erythromycin lactobionate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases erythromycin stearate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 24. Escitalopram increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, and rilpivirine increases escitalopram toxicity by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 27. Esomeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Etravirine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 30. Fexinidazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Fingolimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Rilpivirine increases flecainide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Fluconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 34. Fluoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Fostemsavir and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 36. Rilpivirine increases gemifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Gepirone and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Gilteritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Givinostat and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. 40. Granisetron and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Rilpivirine increases haloperidol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Hydroxyzine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer famotidine at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 45. Ibutilide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Iloperidone and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Indapamide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Indinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Isoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Isoniazid increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Rilpivirine increases isradipine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Itraconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. 53. Ketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for breakthrough fungal infections when azole antifungals are co-administered with rilpivirine. 54. Lansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated. 55. Rilpivirine increases lapatinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Lefamulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 57. Rilpivirine increases levofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Levoketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for breakthrough fungal infections when azole antifungals are co-administered with rilpivirine. 59. Lithium and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Lopinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. 61. Lovotibeglogene autotemcel and rilpivirine may interfere with each other. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 62. Rilpivirine increases lumefantrine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Macimorelin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 64. Magnesium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine.
